The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T02:56:23Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T02:56:46Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-11T02:50:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-11T02:58:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 8 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 17 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T02:59:02Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 26.1% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 35.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 25.1% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.975% {series_before} before it began, 26.125% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 35.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 4,702.30 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T02:56:44Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T02:56:58Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T02:56:58Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T02:57:04Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 02:56:23 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T02:57:09Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 361 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T02:57:10Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:50 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T02:57:10Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T02:57:11Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 11 02:51 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T02:57:13Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T02:57:13Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T02:57:13Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes 23 {T11.3} seconds before 02:56:23 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T02:57:13Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 126 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T02:57:16Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T02:57:16Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T02:57:16Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 02:57:16 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T02:57:20Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T02:57:21Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T02:57:23Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1, moved from OFF to ON
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T02:57:30Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 02:58 {T19.2} - up to 156s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T02:59:01Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 02:58 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-11T02:59:02Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-11T02:59:02Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [legacy-checkout-fallback] ON and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-11T03:00:25Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/539

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-11T02:50:38Z {P1.1} flag-toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G153f] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 {G153f.1} evaluations - 30 {G153f.2} occurrences in 30 {G153f.3} minutes, 02:20–02:49 {G153f.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 38 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 30 {G46bc.2} minutes, 02:20–02:49 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 02:20–02:56 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 35.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 02:55 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 5 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 18 {Gad41.2} minutes, 02:22–02:39 {Gad41.3}
  - [G7ad6] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 70 {G7ad6.1} / on 130 {G7ad6.2} - 200 {G7ad6.3} evaluations - 1 {G7ad6.4} occurrence in 1 {G7ad6.5} minute, 02:50 {G7ad6.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 02:50–02:56 {G5309.3}
  - [G7037] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 {G7037.1} evaluations - 6 {G7037.2} occurrences in 6 {G7037.3} minutes, 02:51–02:56 {G7037.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off at 2026-11-11T02:50:38Z {C1.1}. Account page requests then failed with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to about 28-35% {C1.3}. No code or config was deployed. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` builds the list of purchases with `in_current_month` set, then divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by that list's length. When the list is empty, that is a division by zero. An empty list is normal: it covers any shopper who has bought before but not this month, which `tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py` calls "the ordinary case". `render_spend_summary` sends a request to this function whenever `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false. So every request in that slice, for a shopper with no purchases this month, raised `ZeroDivisionError`. `serve_account_page` in `src/io_shop/account_page.py` catches it at its boundary and turns it into a failed page. The flag change only changed how many requests took that path. The division itself was always wrong.
      
      The fix: if nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0 {F1.1}, meaning nothing spent per item this month. Otherwise it divides exactly as before. The return type stays `int`, so the function signature, `render_spend_summary` and its callers are unchanged. The lifetime average is untouched. Its divisor can still be zero for an account with no purchases at all, and the existing test that expects that error to reach the caller still holds. Errors are not hidden anywhere else: only the empty-month case is handled, and it is handled with a value rather than an exception.
      
      The tests: in `tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py` I added two. One calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` directly, and the other goes through `render_spend_summary(use_monthly_summary=True)`. Both use a shopper with past purchases but none this month and assert the figure is 0 {F1.2}. Both are written to raise `ZeroDivisionError` against the current code.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #539 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and it does not handle the case where that list is empty, which is the ordinary case for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. With legacy-checkout-fallback off, more account page requests went through `render_spend_summary`'s monthly path into this division, raised ZeroDivisionError, and `serve_account_page` turned each one into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching off a feature setting sent more shoppers' account pages through a spending calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases.
still_at_risk: Account page requests that still reach the monthly spend summary could fail for shoppers with no purchases this month, and switching legacy-checkout-fallback off again would bring the same failures back.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of requests answered with server errors rose, and the service logged failed account page requests and warnings about the account page error rate. (cites AL1; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Those account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, and the account page turned each error into a failed page. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
causal_chain 3: At {P1.1} admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off. In the onset minute some account page requests already read the flag as off, every minute after that all of them did, and the ZeroDivisionError failures start in that same onset minute. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7ad6, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7037, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: Some other flag change: the flag provider's history held a single change by anyone but Argus in the hour it read, and that change is this toggle. (cites T15, under "What Argus did, in order"; P1, under "Changes to production it read")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 3: Shoppers closing the connection: those errors were already logged before the onset, at a time when the flag was on and account pages rendered normally. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G153f, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: With the flag off, more account page requests went through render_spend_summary's monthly spend path, where average_spend_per_item_this_month divides by the number of this month's purchases, so it fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: No test was seen that covered average_spend_per_item_this_month, or render_spend_summary's monthly path, for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. The test file itself calls that the ordinary case.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A test with that shopper would have hit the division by zero, so the fault could have been fixed before the flag change exposed it to shoppers.
contributing_factors 2: The production change to legacy-checkout-fallback went from a share of requests to all of them almost at once. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The failures would have stayed within a small slice of requests, and the change would have been halted before it reached every shopper.
contributing_factors 3: No check was seen that exercised account pages with legacy-checkout-fallback off before it was switched off in production.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages would have been seen failing with the flag off before the change was made to production.
action_items 1: Make changes to io-shop feature flags roll out to a small share of requests first, and halt and revert them automatically when the error rate rises.
action_items 2: Add a CI test that renders io-shop account pages with each feature flag both on and off, using a shopper with past purchases but none this month.
action_items 3: Require that the flag-state account page test passes before a flag on io-shop can be changed in production.
action_items 4: Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called in to respond.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
